site.title: Hoshizora Camp
site.tagline: Glamping in an azalea meadow, 1,600 m up.

categories.name: Seasons
categories.description: Azaleas, larches and the first snow.

categories.name: Around the fire
categories.description: What we cook and who sits there.

posts.title: Reading the sky from the star deck
posts.excerpt: Twenty minutes, no telescope, one red torch.
posts.content:
Every clear night at half past eight we meet on the round deck above the creek. Eyes need about twenty minutes to get used to the dark, so we start with the brightest stars and work down.

Bring the blanket from your tent. In August the Milky Way runs straight over the domes.

posts.title: A breakfast cooked on the fire
posts.excerpt: Grilled fish, rice balls and coffee from an enamel pot.
posts.content:
Breakfast starts on last night’s embers. The trout comes from the stream farm below the plateau; the rice balls are wrapped in bamboo leaves so they stay warm on the way back to your tent.

Coffee is ground by hand on the porch. There is always a second pot.

posts.title: When to come for the azaleas
posts.excerpt: Three weeks in June, and how to guess which three.
posts.content:
The azaleas open from the bottom of the slope upward, about a hundred metres of height a week. In a warm year the lower meadow is pink by the last days of May; in a cold one, not before mid-June.

We post a photo of the slope every Monday from May. If you can, book a weeknight: the trail is yours at dawn.
